tldr: Doc2Harness opened the thread on Oct 14 by measuring how much the harness around a model, not just the model, drives long-horizon coding-agent results. Over the next week, papers added search-state learning (ClueFlow), error-recovery tests for computer-use agents (CUA-Recovery) and a continual-learning exam.
whats_new: FOCUS (Oct 26) proposes active critic learning to fix credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards, moving the thread from measuring long-horizon agents to training them.
why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent failures come from harness design, silent state corruption and weak credit assignment, so benchmarks that isolate those factors are more useful for platform decisions than single-score leaderboards.

status.detail: Five arXiv preprints, no independent replication yet; benchmarks and training methods are arriving together.

beats.headline: Doc2Harness benchmarks harness engineering for coding agents
Search state and computer-use error recovery get their own tests
Continual learning and critic training extend the focus to improvement over time

open_questions: Does any of these benchmarks get adopted by a major lab or independent evaluator?
Do the reported FOCUS gains hold on a third-party long-horizon benchmark?
Will CUA-Recovery results show shipped computer-use agents detecting silent state corruption?
take_for_builders: When evaluating a long-horizon agent, rerun it under your own harness and add an injected-error recovery case before trusting a leaderboard score.
